additional_inputs: https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07006v1#S3: section introduction, Lemma3.1, Theorem3.4 (3.1)-(3.3), Lemma3.5 and weighted calculation immediately following it

whole_module_review.private_helper_analysis: Reviewed the entire private theorem statement and every proof line, not merely the exported conclusions. It assumes h>=0, beta h<=1 and the global quadratic upper model at the gradient symbol. Evaluating that model at s=x-h grad f(x) gives f(s)-f(x)<=-h||g||^2+(beta/2)h^2||g||^2. Multiplying beta h<=1 by h||g||^2>=0 proves descent. No beta>=0 or C1 premise is required for this purely algebraic implication from the already supplied upper model. In both public consumers C1 guarantees the gradient is the genuine derivative, recovering the intended source calculus setting. The helper is explained explicitly in both lesson proof chains, as an implementation of Lemma3.1 rather than an independently registered theorem.

independent_math_checks.energy: The signed alpha chord inequality and C1 imply f(z)>=f(x)-<g,x-z>+(alpha/2)||x-z||^2. Multiply by 2h>=0, combine private descent and the exact norm expansion; h^2||g||^2 cancels. No alpha>=0, beta>=0, comparator optimality, or gap sign is used.
independent_math_checks.recurrence: With actual iterates X(n+1)=T(Xn), u_n=||Xn-z||^2 and g_n=f(Xn)-f(z), get u_(n+1)<=q u_n-2h g_(n+1) and g_(n+1)<=g_n. The forced recurrence permits signed -2h g_(n+1) and requires nonnegative coefficient q.
independent_math_checks.weights: For k<N, g_N<=g_(k+1); multiplication by -2h<=0 reverses this inequality. Multiplication by q^(N-(k+1))>=0 then preserves it. Summing, reversing k and discarding u_N>=0 gives precisely 2h S_N g_N<=q^N u0. No bound q<=1 is needed.
independent_math_checks.endpoints: N=0 has S0=0, q^0=1 and yields 0<=||x0-z||^2. h=0 gives T=id, q=1 and a zero left coefficient. q=0 gives S_N=1 and q^N=0 for N>=1 without reciprocal evaluation. q=1 gives S_N=N. q>1, possible with negative alpha, is valid though not a decaying optimization rate.
independent_math_checks.source_comparison: Setting E to Euclidean space, retaining the source C2/nonnegative-modulus hypotheses, choosing h in [0,1/beta] on beta>0 and choosing z=xstar recovers the selected source statements. Arbitrary z is explicitly permitted by source (3.3). The finite weighted bound extends Lemma3.5 positive-A inverse proof to q=0 through a product-form recurrence.
independent_math_checks.normalized_rate_boundary: For h>0, N>=1 and 0<q<1, divide the weighted bound and use S_N=(1-q^N)/(1-q), 1-q=alpha h to obtain alpha R^2/[2(q^(-N)-1)]. For alpha=0, h>0, N>=1, S_N=N yields R^2/(2Nh). These algebraic consequences are not separately published/registered by either binding, and singular h=0, N=0, q=0 or q=1 are not interpreted through the source inverse formula.

counterexamples.descent_missing_nonnegative_step: Take f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1. The printed h<=1/beta holds; T(1)=2 and f(2)-f(1)=3/2 exceeds -(h/2)|grad f(1)|^2=1/2.
counterexamples.general_comparator_energy_missing_nonneg: Take f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=1/2,beta=1,h=-1,x=0,z=1. This f is alpha-strongly convex and beta-smooth. T(0)=0; ||T(0)-1||^2+2h(f(T(0))-f(1))=2 while (1-alpha h)||0-1||^2=3/2. Thus the printed arbitrary-comparator claim fails.
counterexamples.general_comparator_weighted_missing_nonn: Same f,alpha,beta,h, take x0=0,z=1,N=2. q=3/2, g_N=-1/2, S2=5/2. Left side is 5/2 while right side is 9/4. This concerns the general-comparator extension, not a claim that the minimizer weighted inequality itself fails for negative h.
